model: Distributable cash from JV/associate portfolio, capitalised at cost of equity (engine route; investment-holding company)

equity_bridge.note: H1 FY2026 balance sheet: bank deposits and cash 45,268 less bank loans (815 current + 1,948 non-current) = 2,763; net cash 42,505. Undiscounted -- treated as a surplus asset held today, not a future flow. Management has not committed a timeline for deployment (new acquisitions) or return (special dividend); this valuation is agnostic between the two uses and simply adds the cash at face value, which is conservative versus assuming value-accretive M&A redeployment.

historical_growth.notes: revenue_*_cagr and fcf_*_cagr are both computed on the reconstructed distributable-cash series (JV+associate dividends + loan interest + treasury interest, net of cash tax) -- HK$5,748m FY2020 -> HK$5,012m FY2025 (5yr) and HK$5,825m FY2022 -> HK$5,012m FY2025 (3yr) -- because neither statutory revenue (which is 85% understated, see inputs.base_revenue_basis) nor statutory FCF (a parent-only operating cash flow line, see inputs.reported_fcf_note) represents the cash the business actually generates. The mild decline reflects falling shareholder-loan interest income as JVs/associates pay down parent loans (1,380 in FY2017 -> 722 in FY2025) more than offsetting dividend growth; it is a genuine, mild secular headwind separate from the UKPN sale, and is one reason the base case does not assume strong organic growth even before the UKPN haircut. EPS and equity CAGRs are computed on the full 5-year Metrics.csv EPS/ShareholdersEquity series and both include one full year (FY2025) of pre-sale ordinary earnings, so they are unaffected by the FY2026 UKPN gain.

scenario_narratives.base: Power Assets loses UKPN's recurring contribution from FY2026 (a judgemental haircut on the FY2025 base) but the remaining portfolio -- HK Electric, the residual UK gas networks (NGN, WWU, Seabank, Phoenix), and a growing Australian book (SA Power Networks, VPN/UE, AGN, Dampier Bunbury) -- grows modestly as new regulatory price-control periods with higher allowed returns come into effect through FY2026-2027. Management deploys only a modest, rising share of ongoing cash flow into new stakes (no committed pipeline as of H1 2026), so most of the recurring flow continues to be distributed as dividends. The HK$42.5bn net cash from the UKPN sale sits separately as a real balance-sheet asset, added once at face value rather than assumed to be redeployed at above-market returns.
scenario_narratives.bull: UKPN's loss turns out to have been a smaller share of the UK book than the base case assumes, the remaining regulated portfolio benefits fully from the new price-control periods and from AI/data-centre and EV-driven demand growth cited by management, and the enlarged net-cash position is deployed faster and more successfully into new accretive regulated-infrastructure stakes in partnership with CKI/CKA -- exactly the strategy management has articulated but not yet executed or timed.
scenario_narratives.bear: UKPN's loss turns out to have been a larger share of the UK book than the base case assumes, the net cash sits largely idle for an extended period earning only deposit yields while heightened UK/Australian foreign-investment screening slows new deal-making, the structural decline in shareholder-loan interest continues, and one or more of the pending regulatory determinations disappoints (as UKPN's own FY2025 result did, from prior inflation-recovery unwinding). No solvency risk -- this is a stagnant, cash-heavy balance sheet earning a low return on the idle portion, not a survival case.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Power Assets is valued on the cash it actually receives from its JV/associate portfolio -- dividends plus shareholder-loan interest -- capitalised at the HKD cost of equity, because that flow is already net of financing (there is no further debt layer to apply at the parent) and because the group's own accounting profit (equity-accounted share of JV earnings, much of it retained at the JV level rather than distributed) is not the same as cash available to Power Assets shareholders. The UK Power Networks sale (completed May 2026, HK$44.8bn cash, HK$11.3bn accounting gain) is treated as a one-off balance-sheet event, not a run-rate: the resulting HK$42,505m net cash is added once at face value via the equity bridge, and the projected flow excludes both the disposal gain and UKPN's future contribution, replacing FY2025's pre-sale distributable cash of HK$5,208m with a haircut base year that removes UKPN and then grows modestly from the remaining, still-regulated portfolio. This is deliberately conservative on two fronts: the net cash is not assumed to be redeployed at above-market returns (it is added at face value, not compounded), and the reinvestment path assumes only a modest, rising share of ongoing cash flow is deployed into new acquisitions, consistent with management's own stated lack of a committed pipeline or timeline as of the H1 2026 results.
key_risks_to_valuation: UKPN-only split of the UK segment's HK$3,210m FY2025 profit contribution was not separately disclosed; the -14%/-16%/-22% year-1 haircuts across bull/base/bear bound rather than pin down this figure, and it is the single largest driver of the valuation spread between scenarios.

Capital allocation of the HK$42.5bn net cash is entirely undetermined as of H1 2026 (no committed special dividend or acquisition pipeline); the model is deliberately agnostic between the two uses by adding the cash at face value rather than assuming either path, but a value-destructive deployment (overpaying for an acquisition) or a prolonged idle-cash period would both be worse than this valuation assumes, while a well-timed special dividend or accretive deal would not itself change the intrinsic value (cash converts to cash or to an equally-valued asset) but WOULD change the realised return timeline for shareholders.

Discount rate: the flow is terminal-heavy at an 8.0% cost of equity typical of a capitalised annuity-style model; a 1pp move in the discount rate has an outsized effect on the recurring-flow component (though the HK$42.5bn cash floor is discount-rate-invariant, providing a partial valuation cushion).

Nearly all profit and cash flow depends on regulator goodwill across multiple jurisdictions (Ofgem, AER/ESCOSA, HK Scheme of Control); the base case assumes the already-flagged favourable resets (NGN/WWU, SA Power Networks, VPN/UE) materialise roughly as disclosed, and any clawback or adverse surprise (as UKPN itself experienced in FY2025) would compress the recurring flow further.

Currency translation: results are earned in GBP/AUD/CAD/NZD/EUR/THB/RMB and consolidated in HKD; this model does not separately stress FX, relying instead on the historical distributable-cash series (which already embeds realised FX effects) as the base.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance v8 chart API at inputs.price_as_of.
data_sources.financials: 0006.HK_Metrics.csv / core_metrics and kpis (FY2017-FY2025 + H1 FY2026); 0006.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt segment commentary (UK/Australia/HK Electric profit contributions), balance sheet and note 12 (no share option scheme); 0006.HK_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt balance sheet (cash, bank loans, net assets) and UKPN disposal notes.
data_sources.qualitative: 0006.HK_Analysis.json (2026-09-26); FY2025 Annual Report business review and H1 2026 Interim Results commentary on the UKPN/UK Rails disposals and capital-allocation stance.

inputs.base_revenue_basis: FY2025 pre-tax cash actually received by the parent from its JV/associate portfolio: JV dividends 2,958 + associate dividends 1,423 + shareholder-loan interest from JVs/associates 722 + treasury interest income 105 = 5,208 (kpis: DividendsReceivedJV, DividendsReceivedAssociates, LoanInterestIncomeJVAssociates, InterestIncome, FY2025). This is the 'revenue' the engine's growth path compounds -- NOT the HK$771m statutory revenue line (which is almost entirely the shareholder-loan interest and excludes the dividends, so it understates the true cash engine by ~85%), and NOT the HK$6,236m equity-accounted net profit (which includes JV/associate earnings retained at the JV level and never received in cash, plus the FY2025 profit contains no one-off; the FY2026 profit does, from the UKPN gain, and is explicitly excluded -- see notes).
inputs.share_count_basis: 2,131m shares in issue at 30 June 2026 (H1 FY2026 balance sheet); basic = diluted throughout the history (FY2025 AR: 'No share option scheme is in operation', note 12). Held FLAT: no equity compensation, no buybacks in the 9-year history (ShareRepurchases = 0 every period).
inputs.net_debt_note: Deliberately ZERO. The flow being capitalised is cash ALREADY received by the parent net of the (near-zero) parent-level operating costs and cash tax -- there is no further financing charge to apply, so net debt is not subtracted from the capitalised value (dcf-methods SKILL.md: never subtract net debt after capitalising a post-financing flow). The Group's HK$42,505m NET CASH (not net debt) at 30 June 2026 is a real, undeployed balance-sheet asset that the projected cash flow does NOT capture (the flow only projects JV/associate distributions, not a return of this cash pile), so it is added once via equity_bridge below, not here.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2025 owner cash flow to parent = base_revenue 5,208 less FY2025 cash tax paid 196 (kpis CashTaxesPaid) = 5,012. Parent staff costs (36) and other admin are immaterial (<0.5% of the flow) and are folded into the margin path rather than tracked separately.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Metrics.csv FreeCashFlow (883, FY2025) is parent-only operating cash flow from the cash flow statement and does NOT include the JV/associate dividends or loan interest received, which the cash flow statement nets differently; it understates the true distributable flow by ~4.7x and is not used anywhere in this model.
inputs.interest_income_note: Treasury interest income (105 FY2025) is already INSIDE base_revenue (it is part of what the parent actually receives in cash) and is not deducted separately, because the matching asset (the cash balance that earns it) is added via equity_bridge rather than subtracted as debt -- the excluded-income/matching-asset rule is satisfied by including the income and adding the asset once, not by excluding the income.
inputs.sbc_source: No share option scheme in operation (FY2025 AR note 12); SBC is genuinely zero, not merely undisclosed.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Discount rate is a COST OF EQUITY (not a WACC): the flow capitalised is cash already received by the parent, net of parent-level cost and tax, with no further financing layer, so no debt/equity blend applies (dcf-methods SKILL.md non-FCF-models section). HKD long rates track USD closely under the Linked Exchange Rate System: HKD 10-year proxy ~3.8% + 5.0% equity risk premium x beta 0.85 (regulated-monopoly cash flows are lower-beta than the funds-manager/developer names in this folder that use beta 1.0, e.g. CHC.AX's 10.0%; a full percentage point below EBO.NZ's 8.5% AUD cost of equity would be too aggressive given 0006.HK's genuine M&A-execution and JV-governance risk, so beta is held at 0.85 rather than pushed lower) = 8.05%, rounded to 8.0%. One rate across all three scenarios; portfolio-concentration and execution risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked onto the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Immaterial: parent-level lease liabilities are HK$5m (30 June 2026) against HK$42.5bn net cash; excluded from the model.
inputs.nci_treatment: Not applicable at the parent level -- Power Assets' consolidated statement has no NCI; the group's own economic interest in each JV/associate is already reflected in the equity-accounted share-of-profit and cash distributions received (e.g. 33.37% of HK Electric Investments), so no further minority adjustment is needed.
inputs.tax_note: Cash tax paid / cash received ranged 0.7%-6.5% over FY2017-FY2025 (kpis CashTaxesPaid vs the reconstructed cash-in series), trending up in FY2024 (6.5%) and FY2025 (3.8%) versus a 1-2% norm in FY2017-2022. Modelled at 4.0% flat in base, reflecting the recent higher-tax years rather than the older low-tax norm (conservative).
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE: Power Assets earns almost all profit as equity-accounted share of JV/associate results (dcf-methods SKILL.md routing table has no single row that fits an investment-holding company whose flow is JV dividends rather than consolidated FCF or AFFO; it is closest in spirit to the REIT/distributable-profit row -- capitalise the flow the business actually produces, at the rate appropriate to whom it accrues, never re-subtract net debt from an already-post-financing flow -- adapted for a JV/associate dividend stream instead of AFFO). The engine's 'revenue' is therefore CASH RECEIVED from JVs/associates (dividends + shareholder-loan interest) plus treasury interest, not consolidated revenue or equity-accounted profit; 'EBITDA margin' is ~100% minus the (near-zero) parent operating cost; 'capex' is modelled as cash RETAINED rather than distributed, i.e. net reinvestment into new acquisitions -- held low in the base case because management has stated no committed acquisition pipeline as of the H1 2026 report ('cash is king', strict investment criteria, no timeline given for either M&A or a special dividend). UKPN SALE TREATED AS A STRUCTURAL ONE-OFF: the HK$11,286m disposal gain and the HK$44,840m cash proceeds are EXCLUDED from the projected flow entirely (they are a balance-sheet event, captured once via equity_bridge as the resulting net cash, not as a recurring earnings item) and the FY2026 H1 profit spike (HK$14,704m) is NOT used as a base year. FY2025 (last full pre-sale year, HK$5,208m pre-tax cash-in) is the base, with the year-1 (FY2026) growth rate carrying an explicit UKPN-loss haircut (-14% to -22% across scenarios) to remove UKPN's recurring contribution going forward, since the UK segment's HK$3,210m FY2025 profit contribution (of which UKPN was described by management as historically 'one of the largest and highest-quality contributors') no longer includes it -- NGN, WWU, Seabank, Phoenix Energy and UK Renewables remain. The exact UKPN-only split of the UK segment was not separately disclosed in the annual report's segment note, so the haircut is a bounded judgement (roughly half to two-thirds of the UK bucket), not a precise figure; this is the single largest source of uncertainty in the base case and is flagged in valuation_philosophy.key_risks_to_valuation. NET CASH TREATMENT: HK$42,505m (30 June 2026) is added once, undiscounted, via equity_bridge as a surplus balance-sheet asset -- it is NOT run through the WACC/growth machinery (it is not itself a growing cash-generating flow) and net_debt is held at zero throughout to avoid double-counting the same cash position twice.

bear.growth_rationale: UKPN-loss haircut is at the deep end of the plausible range (-22%, i.e. UKPN was a larger share of the UK segment than the base case assumes). Cash sits largely idle at low HKD/AUD/USD deposit yields for an extended period (no committed deployment timeline, heightened foreign-investment screening in the UK/Australia constrains new deals per management's own risk disclosure), the structural decline in shareholder-loan interest continues unmitigated, and one or more adverse regulatory resets (echoing UKPN's own softer FY2025 result from prior inflation-recovery unwinding) offset the positive determinations already locked in elsewhere. No solvency question arises -- the Group carries net cash, not net debt -- so this is a stagnant-earnings-mix case, not a survival case.
bear.capex_rationale: Minimal reinvestment: cash accumulates rather than being deployed, consistent with the bear narrative of a prolonged 'idle cash' period and no accretive new acquisitions; nearly all of the recurring flow continues to be paid out as dividends.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 (year 1) removes UKPN's recurring contribution from the FY2025 base: a judgemental haircut of -16% (see inputs.notes on the bounded UKPN-only split), leaving cash-in of ~HK$4,375m. FY2027-2029 (+3.0-4.0%) capture the new regulatory price-control periods already determined or in train: NGN/WWU higher allowed returns from Dec-2025, SA Power Networks' 2025-30 determination (+33% nominal revenue over the period), VPN/UE/AGN-SA's new 5-year period from 1 July 2026, and continued HK Electric stability -- broadly offsetting the structurally declining loan-interest line. Growth fades to a 2.0% terminal rate, below long-run inflation, reflecting that most of the portfolio is mature regulated infrastructure with periodic (not perpetual) real growth in allowed revenue, and that management has stated no committed new-acquisition pipeline that would lift the growth path further.
base.margin_rationale: Parent-level operating cost (staff costs HK$36m FY2025 plus other admin) is under 1% of the FY2025 cash-in of HK$5,208m; margin held at 96% throughout to leave headroom for modest cost inflation at a 13-16-employee holding company with no operating leverage either way.
base.capex_rationale: Models cash RETAINED rather than distributed to shareholders, i.e. net reinvestment funding new JV/associate stakes -- not physical capex (the parent owns no operating assets to maintain). Held low (3-8% of the flow) in the base case because management has explicitly not committed to a deal pipeline or timeline as of H1 2026 ('cash is king', strict investment criteria); the path rises modestly over the horizon on the assumption that SOME of the enlarged net-cash position is gradually deployed into new regulated-infrastructure stakes at ordinary (not extraordinary) returns, consistent with the historical near-100% payout ratio (DPS HK$2.82 vs distributable cash per share ~HK$2.35-2.77) continuing to dominate capital allocation. The HK$42.5bn net cash itself is NOT modelled as being deployed here -- it sits in equity_bridge at face value; this capex path only affects the modest ongoing retention out of the recurring flow.

bull.growth_rationale: UKPN-loss haircut is at the shallow end of the plausible range (-14%, i.e. UKPN was a smaller share of the UK segment than the base case assumes). The enlarged net-cash position is deployed successfully and faster into new regulated-infrastructure acquisitions in mature markets (management's stated priority: renewables/sustainable energy, continued CKI/CKA co-investment), each accretive from year 1, on top of the same regulatory tailwinds as base (NGN/WWU, SA Power Networks, VPN/UE, AGN). AI/data-centre and EV-driven demand growth (cited by management) lifts network capex and volumes faster than the regulatory floor across the UK/Australian portfolio.
bull.capex_rationale: Faster, more confident deployment of the net-cash pile into new stakes (higher retention early, funding the higher growth path), fading as the portfolio matures; still modest relative to the HK$42.5bn one-off cash addition sitting separately in equity_bridge.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 16x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default 25/50/25. Held at the default rather than skewed: the single largest uncertainty (how much of the UK segment's profit UKPN represented) is genuinely two-sided and is already expressed as a wide bear/bull spread in the year-1 haircut (-22% to -14%) rather than in the weights. Management's own stated approach (disciplined, no committed timeline for either M&A or a special dividend, 'cash is king') is itself a hedge against both an overly optimistic bull (fast, confident redeployment) and an overly pessimistic bear (permanently idle cash) -- the base case, in which some but not most of the flow is retained and deployed at ordinary returns, is the most likely outcome given management's demonstrated caution.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
